events.text_en: Mạc Quy Khư comes out of Phù Tang Cảnh with his root burned through by its ten suns and an unglazed vase in his arms that is colder than the sea.
The ice swordsman Hoắc Hàn Quang asks Mạc Quy Khư how the Hóa Thần tribulation is lived through, and is told: with empty hands. He lays his sword on the stone of his cave and goes north.
A Wind-rooted swordsman with no robe comes down the ore road past Không Thanh Khoáng, and a ninety-year-old miner with a pure Metal root puts down his pick and follows him.
At the door of Lương Lạc Mai's abode her disciple hears two flutes playing the falling-plum tune. One stops as the door opens. She closes it again.
The traveller seen off from Tống Khách Thị is Quách Lĩnh Thù, the founder of Phất Y Cốc, 110 years after he hung his robe in his valley. He leaves his sword with his disciple.
Cao Đan Hà's herb girl climbs back to her master's abode in the winter and closes it on the furnace, the pill and the body.
Yến Tang Điền, the last of Cô Phàm Các, crosses to Dục Nhật Đảo to ask the hermit one thing, and is given nothing.
The sword sage Tư Không Hạc Niên leaves the boy he taught at Hàn Mai and swears to teach no one.
Lightning splits a fishing boat in the strait; the blind man of the pool walks into the sea and carries out the fisher's daughter.
The hermit of Dục Nhật Đảo does not wake for the spring question. His ferryman answers it in his voice.
